title: Same Trick
intro: The same trick facing east, south, west and north. A function uses [i]relative[/i] moves, so it works whichever way the robot faces. Which chunk is worth naming?
cs_note: Relative moves make a function [b]portable[/b]: it doesn't care which way you face. Picking the right chunk to abstract is the real skill: a slightly bigger chunk can make the rest of the program much simpler.
hints: The thing that repeats isn't just the dodge. Look one tile wider on each side.
Each side of the square is A, A, then a right turn.

A is the same move-dodge-move as in Copy, Paste, Regret. It uses only relative turns, so it works facing any direction. A repeat 3 times of A, A, turn_right() walks three sides of the square; then A, turn_right(), move() and a last A finish the path to the exit.
